result.summary: Adds a C API endpoint and C++ wrapper to libbitcoinkernel for validating a block without requiring a complete local UTXO set. A new `ValidateBlock` method is exposed on `ChainstateManager` that executes `CheckBlock`, `ContextualCheckBlock`, and a check-only `ConnectBlock` against a custom `CCoinsViewCache` populated via a user-supplied coin-fetching callback.
result.problem: External consumers of libbitcoinkernel, such as rust-bitcoinkernel or stateless verifiers, cannot validate full blocks without maintaining a complete local chainstate and UTXO database on disk.

open_concerns: ajtowns questioned the callback design, preferring an in-memory CoinsDb container to avoid non-deterministic lookups and expose UTXO deltas
nervana21 noted that ConnectBlock may skip script checks under assumevalid if the block is an ancestor of the assumevalid tip
optout21 noted the need for direct validation unit tests and more realistic test cases supplying all UTXOs
resolved_concerns: Switched from passing raw block undo data or dual arrays to a callback-based coin fetcher

result.card: This PR adds a libbitcoinkernel C API and C++ wrapper to validate blocks against user-supplied coins without requiring a complete local UTXO database. It introduces `ChainstateManager::ValidateBlock`, which runs `CheckBlock`, `ContextualCheckBlock`, and a check-only `ConnectBlock` against a caller-provided coin-fetching callback. This allows external library consumers, such as rust-bitcoinkernel or stateless validators, to verify blocks independently of the node's disk state. Concept is well-supported, but the PR needs a rebase, and open design discussions remain regarding callback consistency versus an in-memory container and script-skipping under assumevalid.
